How an Online Store Became a Cloud and Ad Empire

A decade ago, Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) was mostly an online store with a promising cloud side business. Over the decade that followed, AWS became the dominant profit engine, Prime grew alongside a huge logistics expansion, and advertising turned into a giant that brought in $19.8 billion in Q2 2026 alone, up 26%.

kasinv / iStock Editorial via Getty Images
AMZN Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.

The pandemic sent e-commerce demand surging, and Andy Jassy succeeded Jeff Bezos as CEO in July 2021. Then the bill came due. Amazon overbuilt its fulfillment network, posted its first unprofitable year since 2014 in 2022, and the stock fell roughly 50%.

AI Pushed AWS Back Into High Gear

Cost discipline under Jassy brought margins back, and AI demand revived cloud growth. AWS revenue rose 36.7% to $42.2 billion in Q2 2026, its fastest growth in 18 quarters. The company's AI and chips businesses each passed run rates of more than $25 billion.

Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN | AMZN Price Prediction) runs the world's biggest cloud platform, and that cloud is speeding up again. AWS revenue reached $42.23B in Q2 FY26, up 37% YoY. That was its fastest growth in 18 quarters.

jetcityimage / iStock Editorial via Getty Images

The stock is up 13.97% this year, which still trails what the business is doing. CEO Andy Jassy now says AWS could become "a trillion-dollar annual revenue business for us in time." So can Amazon reach $500 per share by 2030?

AMZN Price Target — 24/7 Wall St.
Spending Fears Are Holding Amazon Back Right Now

Capex is the concern. Amazon raised its 2026 cash capex estimate to roughly $220 billion, up from about $200 billion, and cited higher memory costs. Free cash flow turned negative at -$7.6B TTM. Q3 guidance calls for only 9-12% sales growth, partly because Prime Day moved into Q2.

CNBC this week called it a "stumbling stock" that needs a path back to record highs. Shares sit at $262.59, below the 52-week high of $287.20. The past week (+1.74%) and month (+3.69%) show only a small rebound. With a beta of 1.456, the stock tends to amplify market moves.

Analysts Are Bullish, but Their Targets Stop Too Soon

Wall Street's consensus target is $331.46. The ratings include 16 Strong Buys, 43 Buys, 2 Holds, along with 0 Sells. The model puts shares at $334.91, a 27.54% gain. The bear case sits at $287.36, while the bull case reaches $386.57. Confidence in the model is 0.7, which is fairly high.

NEW YORK, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Egan-Jones recommends that shareholders of Ethan Allen vote FOR all five dissident nominees put forward by DGB Investment on the WHITE card at the company's November 4 annual meeting, according to its commentary on the proxy contest. The piece applies a lesson from Warren Buffett's years in textiles to the 94-year-old furniture maker.

Egan-Jones Ratings Co.

Buffett took control of Berkshire Hathaway in 1965, when it was a New England textile maker, and kept the mills running for twenty years before closing the business in 1985. He later wrote that he should have quit sooner. Egan-Jones cites his general rule that in a commodity business it is impossible to be a lot smarter than your dumbest competitor.

Egan-Jones finds the furniture business largely commoditized, with easily copied designs, low brand recognition and little pricing power. Competitors include Costco, Wayfair, IKEA and Amazon, as well as resale platforms such as Facebook Marketplace. Ethan Allen has sought to move toward the upper end of the market through customized furniture, but the commentary concludes that it does not qualify as designer furniture.

The financial record shows the strain. Ethan Allen's sales have fallen four years in a row, and because its stores and factories are largely fixed costs, the lost sales cut deeply into profit. In fiscal 2026 the company paid more in dividends than it generated in free cash flow, and two weeks after the contest began it declared a $3.00 special dividend, about $76 million.

Egan-Jones contrasts this with Williams-Sonoma, which succeeded by designing its own products, building distinct brands and leading early in e-commerce. DGB's slate includes the former chief commercial officer of Wayfair and eBay's former chief strategy officer. Its plan starts with winning new customers online, along with a brand refresh, a new assortment and a store-by-store review, and DGB plans to name an interim CEO on November 4 if it wins.

Unlike Buffett's mills, Ethan Allen still has a known brand, its own factories, a design service and a debt-free balance sheet. Egan-Jones believes the DGB nominees are better placed to put those assets to work, and recommends voting FOR all five on the WHITE card.

title: Q3 Earnings Season: Strong Base, Higher Revision Trends, and Promising 2027 Outlook
detail:
Q3 Earnings Season: Strong Base, Higher Revision Trends, and Promising 2027 Outlook
Sheraz Mian

AMZN

MU
NVDA

We have a third of S&P 500 members on deck to report Q3 results this week, including three Mag 7 members – Alphabet GOOGL and Microsoft MSFT on Wednesday and Amazon AMZN on Thursday. By the end of this week, we will have seen Q3 results from more than 50% of S&P 500 members.

With results from about a quarter of S&P 500 members already out, we see a continuation of the broad-based strength we've seen in the last few reporting cycles. While the growth pace remains strong, it does not compare favorably with other recent periods, particularly when some of the outlier numbers are excluded. Most importantly, the revisions trend remains positive, with estimates for 2026 Q4 and full-year 2027 continuing to rise.

Looking at overall expectations for the quarter, combining the actual results from the 121 S&P 500 members that have reported already with estimates for the still-to-come companies, Q3 earnings are currently expected to increase by +26.2% from the same period last year on +12.2% higher revenues, the 8th straight quarter of double-digit earnings growth for the index.

The Tech sector continues to be a major growth contributor, but the momentum is broad-based, with 14 of the 16 Zacks sectors on track to enjoy positive earnings growth and 6 generating double-digit earnings growth in Q3.

The quarterly chart below details actual results alongside Q3 2026 growth expectations and forward projections.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

As noted earlier, the revisions trend has been positive, sustaining the favorable trend in place for almost a year. Estimates for Q3 increased after the quarter got underway, and we are seeing a similar trend at play for 2026 Q4 estimates, as the chart below shows.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

This positive revision behavior is not new; it extends a tailwind that has been building for nearly a year. The positive revisions were at first concentrated in Technology and, more recently, Energy following Middle East supply disruptions. However, for 2026 Q4 and also what we saw for Q3, the favorable estimate revisions have broadened significantly, rising across 7 of the 16 Zacks sectors—including Industrials, Basic Materials, Finance, Aerospace and Conglomerates alongside Tech and Energy since the start of October.

On the negative side, Q4 estimates have come down since the start of October for 9 sectors, with the major declines at the Transportation, Autos, Consumer Staples, Consumer Discretionary, Construction, and Utilities sectors.
